_about: The executable engines presented by PURPOSE (communications/DESIGN_brief_deliverables.md §D). plain_name is the executive register; analysts/researchers see the engine name. Joined at runtime with the capability registry by src/dossier/catalog.py — an engine missing from the registry is dropped, never shown stale.

groups.title: Test a position
groups.purpose: what can be attacked, what accepting it commits you to

engines.use_when: know where an argument is strong and where it can be attacked — the hidden premises, the weak joints, who bears the burden of proof
engines.yields: claim-by-claim scorecard (claim · evidence · unstated premise · weak joint · attack)

engines.use_when: know what you are really signing up for if you adopt a position, a framework, a pledge
engines.yields: ledger of explicit → implicit commitments, their conflicts, what depends on what, the practical "so what"

engines.use_when: see the tensions a discourse cannot resolve, which side secretly depends on the other, and what it cannot think
engines.yields: map of tensions (tension · positions · what each excludes · how it plays out)

engines.use_when: test claims that rest on "had X not happened…" — which what-ifs hold and which are rhetoric
engines.yields: audit of each counterfactual (the world it assumes · the causal chain · plausibility · abuse pattern)

engines.use_when: know which "must / cannot / could" claims are real necessities and which are emphasis
engines.yields: inventory of necessity/possibility claims with their backing and confusions

groups.title: See the structure
groups.purpose: the template that repeats, the ideas that hold it up

engines.use_when: have several cases or texts and need the one template that repeats across them (and where each case departs from it)
engines.yields: the template's stages with every case mapped onto them; departures flagged

engines.use_when: know which ideas hold the whole thing up — remove it and the argument collapses
engines.yields: ranking of concepts by what depends on them; hub/bridge topology

engines.use_when: know what job each key term is doing (foundation, defence, bridge, conclusion) and where the argument is thin
engines.yields: term-by-job table + vulnerability points

engines.use_when: know which frameworks and lenses the material thinks with, and what each lets you see and not see
engines.yields: inventory of frameworks (where used · what it shows · what it hides · where it came from)

engines.use_when: the material argues by comparison (A vs B, typologies, scales) and you need to know whether the comparisons hold
engines.yields: audit of each comparison (what is transferred · where it breaks · would other criteria reverse it)

engines.use_when: know how a theory was assembled — borrowed pieces, innovations, how it touches evidence
engines.yields: build map of the theoretical framework

engines.use_when: know the kinds of reasoning a text relies on (probabilistic, strategic, normative…) and how rigorously
engines.yields: inventory of reasoning forms with rigor notes

groups.title: Follow the words
groups.purpose: how terms move, get captured, change meaning

engines.use_when: the same term appears across documents or years and you need to know how its meaning shifted
engines.yields: trajectory table (term · meaning in A · meaning in B · what changed · what it now licenses)
engines.fit_note: ok on corpora; designed for prior/current work of one author

engines.use_when: know who took a term and bent it to their purposes — co-optation, capture, borrowed authority
engines.yields: register of appropriations (term · origin · who uses it now · how it was bent · acknowledged?)

engines.use_when: one concept is central and you need its whole neighbourhood — near-synonyms, opposites, boundary cases
engines.yields: field map for 3–5 concepts

engines.use_when: you have per-document concept readings and need one cross-document picture with a verdict
engines.yields: unified concept picture + convergence/divergence + verdict
engines.fit_note: synthesis pass; needs prior phases — only as the last step after a concept engine

engines.use_when: an author or organisation changed its line and you need to see how the change was managed (silent revision, reframing, disavowal)
engines.yields: tactic catalogue with evidence
engines.fit_note: presumes the same author across time (e.g. successive annual reports); off for mixed-author bundles

groups.title: Read it properly
groups.purpose: what a text argues, how it is built, what it hides

engines.use_when: know what each document actually argues, how, and what it foregrounds or suppresses — and, as a last pass, one synthesis across the phases
engines.yields: per-document argument map (thesis · moves · evidence · what is suppressed · key vocabulary)

engines.use_when: how the story is told matters — voice, arc, what the sequencing does to the reader
engines.yields: story-shape reading per document

engines.use_when: know how the authors claim to know what they claim — methods, standpoint, self-awareness — before you rely on them
engines.yields: credibility grounding per document

engines.use_when: know what had to be in place for this argument or practice to emerge, and what it forecloses
engines.yields: enabling/constraining conditions + paths not taken
engines.fit_note: designed around an author's prior work; usable at surface on a corpus

engines.use_when: a single long work (book, long report) needs a map of what each part does and depends on
engines.yields: chapter role map with dependencies and weak points
engines.fit_note: single long work only; off for multi-paper bundles

groups.title: Count and date
groups.purpose: the numbers and the sequence of events as the sources give them, with what each can carry

engines.use_when: you will cite the sources' numbers and need to know what each one is (target, estimate, observation), over what base and period, what claim it carries, and which comparisons hold
engines.yields: quantity ledger (value · unit · of what · period · status · source · claim carried), comparisons with what differs, the figures the argument lacks
engines.fit_note: needs a text with numbers; on a purely conceptual paper it returns a short inventory and says so

engines.use_when: you need the sequence of events as the sources report it and must know which causal links the sources actually support
engines.yields: timeline (event · date · precision · actor · source), causal links (cause → effect · type · asserted or implied · support), coverage and gaps
engines.row_unit: one row per event or link
engines.fit_note: needs dated reporting; a gap is reported as a gap, never as concealment

excluded.why: presumes a selected source thinker and a subject author (Anxiety-of-Influence workflow); no such structure in a corpus dossier
